Good Wednesday afternoon. Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 648 words, a 2½-min. read. Thanks to Amy Stern for copy editing.

 
 
1 big thing: Making sense of cyber mayhem
 
Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Stock: Getty Images

Most Americans are baffled and alarmed by the sudden explosion of technical glitches hitting air travel, banks and work products like Microsoft Outlook. The outages seem genuinely scary and related, Jim VandeHei and Mike Allen write in a "Behind the Curtain" column.

  • So what the hell is going on?

The most likely answer: This is the first true wave of unintended consequences of increasingly powerful artificial intelligence hitting us at once.

🤖 The big picture: In short, AI is exceptionally good at building software, and therefore exceptionally good at spotting and exploiting bugs in large technical, software-based systems.

  • The glitches come from a mix of sources — some innocuous, some scary, including: routine updates to aging infrastructure; humans scrambling to patch vulnerabilities discovered by AI; hackers exploiting existing weaknesses; and bad actors using swarms of AI agents to launch increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks.

That's the new reality that government officials and AI experts believe we're entering.

  • They expect this period of disruption and heightened vulnerability to persist for months, as powerful new AI tools expose weaknesses buried in decades-old systems.
  • The catchphrase gaining currency: "Software Beirut" — a period of cascading failures, many of our own making, that could grow worse before things get better.

🫨 What this means for YOU: Understand the different causes and resist the temptation to panic every time something goes haywire.

  • It's easy to hop on social media and let the algorithm drag you into doomsday thinking.

💵 You should also prepare: Reset and protect your passwords. Keep more cash on hand if possible, in case your bank is down for a day or two. Buy some basic emergency supplies in case power or water do go out.

  • Sadly, we believe this season of glitches and possible cyberattacks will persist. Better to be prepared.

2. 📖 Word of the year
 
Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios. Stock: Getty Images

"Human" is Cambridge Dictionary's word of the year, reflecting the intense debate over AI and its role in our lives.

🤖 Colin McIntosh, the dictionary's lexicographer, tells AP: "AI is changing how we talk about being human."

  • "Fears about what humans may lose when we outsource our thinking have made us reconsider the extent to which we rely on AI: from top mathematicians to teachers of young children."

How a family business uses Claude to stay true to its roots
 
 

Bama Sea Products started in 1977 with two shrimp boats. Today, the Florida-based company competes in a global market using custom tools the team built with Claude to uphold the quality and safety standards the business has always stood for.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
Chinese President Xi Jinping greets President Trump today in Shenzhen, China. Photo: Mandel Ngan/AFP via Getty Images
  1. 🇺🇸 🇷🇺 President Trump plans to meet separately with Russian President Vladimir Putin tomorrow in China, in addition to their already scheduled three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. More from Barak Ravid.
  2. ✈️ Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin defended his weekend flight to a college football game as many travelers were still stuck after Friday's nationwide ground stop. He told a House committee that canceling his trip could have caused confusion. Go deeper.
  3. 🇻🇪 Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is visiting Venezuela to meet with interim authorities, underscoring the Trump administration's efforts to deepen its influence there. Go deeper.
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries embraces House Democratic Whip Katherine Clark (D-Mass.) after today's vote. Photo: Aaron Schwartz/Reuters

🏛️ Democrats voted at a closed-door caucus meeting this morning to nominate Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) as their candidate for speaker, Axios' Andrew Solender reports.

  • It's a symbolic but significant step that suggests Jeffries has the votes to be elected the first Black House speaker on Jan. 3. Go deeper.
 
 
4. 🎮 1 fun thing: GTA VI gets rave reviews
 
The GTA VI trailer plays on multiple computer screens. Photo: Chris Delmas/AFP via Getty Images

Grand Theft Auto VI is getting nearly flawless reviews ahead of its overnight launch, with a stunning 99/100 on score aggregator Metacritic.

  • Rockstar Games' GTA VI — the first entry in the powerhouse franchise in over a decade — is easily the year's most-anticipated video game release. Presales reportedly topped $1 billion.

🕹️ The reviewers say...

  • The Verge: "This is the GTA game the studio has been building toward for its entire existence."
  • IGN: "Frankly, I've never played anything that's hit quite like GTA 6 — and right now I have zero plans to stop playing it."
  • Bloomberg: "Grand Theft Auto VI is, in short, a masterpiece."
